draft.title: Probability density functions
card: A continuous variable can take any value in an interval, such as a height or a waiting time. The chance of one exact value is 0, so we find the chance of a range of values.
A probability density function f(x) is a curve. P(a ≤ X ≤ b) is the area under the curve from x = a to x = b. This area is found by integrating: ∫ f(x) dx from a to b.
A density function must follow two rules. f(x) ≥ 0 for every x, so no area is negative. The total area under the whole curve is 1.
Example: f(x) = 0.25 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 4, and 0 elsewhere. The total area is 0.25 × 4 = 1. P(1 ≤ X ≤ 3) = 0.25 × 2 = 0.5.
draft.remember: For a continuous variable, probability is area under f(x), and the total area is 1.

a.q: f(x) = k for 0 ≤ x ≤ 5, and 0 elsewhere, is a probability density function. What is k?
a.why: The total area must be 1, so the rectangle gives k × 5 = 1 and k = 0.2. Choosing 5 mixes up the width with the height.
a.clue: Set the area of the rectangle equal to 1.

b.q: A waiting time X minutes has f(x) = 0.1 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 10, and 0 elsewhere. What is P(X ≥ 7)?
b.why: The area from x = 7 to x = 10 is 0.1 × 3 = 0.3. The value 0.7 is the area from 0 to 7, which is P(X ≤ 7), so it is the wrong part of the curve.
b.clue: Find the width of the interval from 7 to the end of the curve.

check.summary: No problems found. The card, both questions and both explanations are correct and match the card; the answers are k = 0.2 and P(X ≥ 7) = 0.3.
